title: Probability: The Probability Scale, Single Events and Experiments
seo_title: Sec 2 Probability Worksheets: Free Secondary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: probability as a measure of chance; probability of single events (including listing all the possible outcomes in a simple chance situation to calculate the probability)
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 probability worksheets: the 0 to 1 probability scale, probabilities of single events, P(not A), sample spaces for dice and coins, expected outcomes and relative frequency. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: P(event) = ways it can happen ÷ total outcomes. Probabilities go from 0 to 1.
key_sub: P(not A) = 1 − P(A). Expected number = probability × number of trials.
body_html:
How it works

Probability measures how likely something is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). Write it as a fraction, decimal or percentage.

When all outcomes are equally likely: P(event) = number of ways it can happen ÷ total number of outcomes. The probability of something not happening is 1 − P(it happens).

From an experiment, the relative frequency = number of times it happened ÷ number of trials.

Example

A bag has 3 red and 5 blue counters. Find P(red).

8 counters, 3 are red.

Answer: 3/8

Example

P(late) = 0.15. Find P(not late).

1 − 0.15.

Answer: 0.85

Example

A dice is rolled 300 times. How many 6s would you expect?

1/6 × 300.

Answer: 50

Common mistakes

  • Writing a ratio such as 3 : 5 instead of a probability. It should be 3/8.
  • Using the wrong total: with 3 red and 5 blue, the total is 8, not 5.
  • Forgetting that all the probabilities add up to 1.
  • Thinking a coin “is due” a tail after several heads. Each flip is independent.

faq.a: A line from 0 to 1. 0 means impossible, 0.5 means an even chance and 1 means certain.

faq.q: How do I find the probability of something not happening?
faq.a: Subtract the probability that it happens from 1. If P(rain) = 0.3, then P(no rain) = 0.7.
The fraction of trials in which something happened in an experiment. It is an estimate of the probability, and more trials give a better estimate.
